correctness.rationale: Reconstructed p-morphism forth/back on the edge-below-vertices poset: maximal vertex worlds must map to one of m incomparable tops, and an edge with distinct endpoint colors can map to bottom iff m=2; otherwise components must be monochromatic, yielding b2=2^v and bm=m^c. For m=2, marked bottom edges are precisely graph cuts; each cut has 2^c colorings from component flips, yielding exact polynomial; its support spans binary cut space, whose orthogonal complement is cycle space. All small graphs v+e≤8 were independently enumerated by graph isomorphism and parameters to establish sharp 6/7/8 world thresholds, including 2K2 vs P3+K1 and C4 vs triangle+pendant. Direct enumeration of bounded morphisms and cut weights for 12 graph/fan cases independently confirmed formulas. Unrestricted all-graph argument uses elementary color/lift proof; finite enumeration only sharp boundary.

residual_risks: This result combines two standard elementary mechanisms (vertex coloring and cut/cycle orthogonality); an earlier unindexed modal-logic application or an immediate corollary of a more general source may cover the composite.

final_claim: For Q_G incidence poset with edge elements below vertices and fans F_m, b_2(G)=2^v, b_m(G)=m^c (m≥3), and the edge-marked b2 polynomial equals 2^c times binary cut-space support enumerator, recovering cycle matroid. Same-world-count scalar collisions first at six, marked separation first at eight, and connected scalar collision first at seven.
limitations: Finite simple nonempty graphs, edge below endpoint vertices, all target points distinguished, m≥2, no surjectivity; same-v hypothesis essential for marked matroid equivalence; no arbitrary frame classification.
